author: claude

generation.prompt:
Pixel art WALK CYCLE sprite sheet of the EXACT same character as attached image 1 — a finished pixel-art sprite.
Copy it pixel for pixel in style: same very large chunky pixels, same 16-colour palette, same dark outline,
same proportions (about 4 heads tall), same face. Long wavy golden-blonde hair under a dark thorny crown, a black gown with a high slit flowing into a cape of living flame in ember orange and soot black, gold filigree at the waist and arms, bare legs with gold anklets and black-and-gold heeled sandals, a slender blade of flame over blackened iron held at the image-left side.
Keep decoration as simple as image 1 — do not add new details. Image 3 is only a colour and face reference; do not copy its painterly style.

Sheet layout: portrait canvas 2160 x 3840, 6 frames in a 3 x 2 grid (cell 720 x 1920), read left to right, top to bottom.
In every cell the character is the same size (about 125 pixels tall on the sprite's own pixel grid, each sprite pixel
drawn as a crisp 13 x 13 square), centred horizontally, with both feet on the same baseline near the bottom of the cell.
Every frame faces the same direction as described below. Hard edges only: no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering noise.
Transparent background. No grid lines, no cell borders, no numbers, no labels, no text, no ground, no shadow, no motion lines, no extra characters.
Side three-quarter view walking toward the viewer's right, walking in place (the character does not travel across the cell).

LEGS: the legs are hidden by a long skirt or robe — follow attached image 2 only for where the two feet are and how the hem moves:
frame 1 = NEAR foot forward peeking out in front of the hem, FAR foot behind (only its toe showing at the back of the hem); the hem pushes forward;
frame 2 = feet close, hem settles, body 1 pixel lower; frame 3 = FAR foot swinging forward under the hem, body 1 pixel higher;
frame 4 = the MIRROR of frame 1: FAR foot forward in front of the hem, NEAR foot behind; frame 5 = feet close, body 1 pixel lower;
frame 6 = NEAR foot swinging forward under the hem, body 1 pixel higher. Frames 1 and 4 must clearly show a different foot in front.
The hem sways opposite to the forward foot. The loop 6 -> 1 must be seamless.
